title: When a question's options carry a large tradeoff, the option judge pushes back and asks for a better option
why: Owner ask ask-mw80xweioa (10:05 CST Nov 8): "when question options present large tradeoffs between its choices can that be a trigger for an option judge to push back asking for a better options based solution?"
note: Filed 10:06 CST Nov 8 by triage from the owner's ask on the waiting page. One home: extend the model review that judges every chat and page question (step page-question-judge, hooks/call_judge.py, decision question-form), not a second judge. The judge reads each option's gain and lose; when every option loses something large, it refuses or asks the writer for an option that keeps the gains, before the question reaches the owner. Related: step challenger-page-against (a blind best case against the pick). Open for the building lane: how the judge sizes a large tradeoff, with red cases from past page items. A judge that cries wolf is spent (rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent), so measure its false alarms on past items first. Doing 10:14 CST Nov 8 under owner item 387 a (coordinator 10:11 CST). First act: count the false alarms the judge would raise on past page questions.
